raw.title: Reasoning Quality Matters: Combating Reasoning Collapse in LLM-based Embedding Learning
raw.body: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential for producing context-rich text embeddings for retrieval. Most existing methods either treat embedding learning as passive feature extraction or exploit LLM reasoning through instruction following for better embedding optimization. However, specialization toward embedding objectives can suppress useful reasoning generation or produce retrieval-irrelevant text. We refer to these two forms of degradation as reasoning collapse. To address this issue, we propose CoFree (Collapse-Free Reasoning Embedding), a two-stage framework that progressively integrates LLM reasoning into query and document embedding optimization while preserving reasoning quality. At the first stage, CoFree applies reference-guided supervised fine-tuning to restore the reasoning ability and retain representational strength of the foundation embedding model. At the second stage, we introduce dual rewards, an embedding-oriented reward and a reasoning-oriented reward, to guarantee fine-grained reasoning of the relevance toward the embedding goal in reinforcement learning. This endpoint-coupled optimization transforms embedding learning from static alignment into a high-quality reasoning-guided search process for retrieval. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of CoFree, with CoFree-4B achieving an average absolute improvement of 2.8 nDCG@10 points over Qwen3-Embedding-4B across 22 datasets from MTEB and BRIGHT. Online experiments in a real-world retrieval system further show consistent gains. Code, RTED, and model checkpoints will be made publicly available.

analysis.one_line_summary: LLM 임베딩에 추론 품질 유지해 검색 성능 향상

key_points.point: Embedding 특화가 LLM 추론을 억제해 검색 관련성을 떨어뜨리는 ‘reasoning collapse’ 현상이 발생한다.
CoFree는 참고 기반 지도 학습 후 이중 보상 강화학습으로 추론 품질을 유지하면서 임베딩을 최적화한다.
실험에서 CoFree‑4B가 22개 데이터셋에서 nDCG@10을 평균 2.8점 향상시키며 실서비스에서도 일관된 개선을 보였다.

analysis.positioning: 기존 임베딩 학습은 단순 특징 추출이나 지시 따르기에 머물러 LLM 추론을 손상시켰다. CoFree는 추론‑임베딩을 연계한 두 단계 프레임워크로, 정적 정렬을 넘어 추론‑가이드 검색을 구현한다. 이는 LLM 기반 검색 최적화 흐름에서 추론 품질을 보존하는 새로운 접근이다
production_ideas: LLM 코드 생성 모델에 참고 기반 지도 학습을 적용해 추론 능력을 회복하고 API 특화 성능을 높인다.
추천 시스템 임베딩 학습에 이중 보상 강화학습을 도입해 정확도와 설명 가능성을 동시에 개선한다.
이미지‑텍스트 멀티모달 검색에 CoFree 방식을 적용해 시각적 추론을 유지하면서 임베딩 정렬을 강화한다

raw.title: The last IMO problem AI could not solve
raw.transcript:
[00:00] Before 2024, AI could not answer questions from the International Math Olympiad.
[00:04] But then Google DeepMind made a model that answered four out of the six questions on that year's test.
[00:10] The next year, multiple organizations had models answering every question from that year's contest, except for the last one.
[00:17] And then by this year, prompting reasoning models available to the public would be enough to answer all six.
[00:23] Looking back at 2025, though, that last question was especially interesting.
[00:27] Among the students that were participating in that year's contest, each of whom is a world-class problem solver among the six best in their country, only six out of the 603 participants there got full marks on this question.
[00:39] Here's the question statement itself if you want to pause and read it.
[00:42] The setup involves a very large square grid, where technically the problem describes a 2025 by 2025 grid, but for illustration purposes, I'll show a smaller one.
[00:51] The game is to cover the grid in tiles where the edges of the tiles line up with the grid, and tiles can't overlap with each other, in such a way that every row has exactly one unit square that's not covered, and likewise every column has exactly one unit square that's not covered.
[01:06] The question asks you to find the smallest number of tiles you can use to satisfy this property.
[01:12] And this being the International Math Olympiad, the task is not merely to give a numerical answer or to show what that optimal tiling is.
[01:19] That's part of it, but the bulk of the task is to rigorously prove that every other possible tiling must use more.
[01:25] Solving a problem like this walks you down a beautiful path of intuition and discovery.
[01:31] It's the topic of a long-form video I just posted, so next time you're in the mood to leave the shorts feed and settle into a longer lesson, give it a look.

raw.title: How a Robot Tests an Action Before It Moves
raw.transcript:
[00:00] How can a robot test an action without moving?
[00:03] A world model can predict the outcome.
[00:05] Here's NVIDIA's Ming-Yu Liu.
[00:07] There are three important modeling in robotics: forward dynamics. Given the starting point and the action taken, what would be the future? Predict what's going to happen.
[00:17] Inverse dynamics. Given the visual transition, infer what was the action taken. And policy, what should the robot do to achieve the task?
[00:27] And our result in the paper show that the synergy, one does help the other.
[00:32] Cosmos trains these abilities together.
[00:35] Developers can use it as a virtual testing ground for robots.
[00:39] Instead of setting up a thousand kitchens, you know, you have this close simulator to help you quickly verify the accuracy of your passing model.
raw.body:
How can a robot test an action without moving? NVIDIA's Ming-Yu Liu explains how a world model predicts the outcome first.

Cosmos 3 learns three abilities together: forward dynamics (what happens after an action), inverse dynamics (which action caused a change) and policy (what the robot should do next). The results in the paper show that each one helps the others. The payoff is a closed-loop simulator. Instead of setting up a thousand kitchens, developers can check a robot policy in simulation before trying it for real.

Full interview: https://youtu.be/L6tLBApQN-g

Learn more about Cosmos: https://nvda.ws/4cJoY1S
Explore Cosmos Lab: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos3/

This video is a paid partnership with NVIDIA.
